Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

IL-6 receptor blockade began within one month of attack nadir. Thirteen attacks were treated as acute escalation after inadequate earlier therapy; five represented early initiation of maintenance treatment.
The authors report an EDSS improvement before IL-6 blockade, from a nadir median of 5.0 to a pre-blockade median of 3.5 (P=.001), and a further decrease to 2.0 at three months (P=.03 versus pre-blockade). These are the reported comparison summaries; the packet does not establish the participant subset for every paired comparison. There is no concurrent untreated control group. Explain what the sequence supports and what it leaves unresolved about an acute rescue effect. Address attacks versus patients, the two treatment intentions, the improvement already present before blockade, and why the reported P values do not alone identify a causal effect. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "**Interpretation of the IL-6 Blockade Series**

The reported sequence, nadir median EDSS 5.0, pre-blockade 3.5, three-month 2.0, supports a temporal association between IL-6 receptor blockade and further disability improvement, but it does not establish an acute rescue effect.

Several features limit causal inference. First, the cohort mixes 18 attacks across 17 patients, so one individual contributed two attacks; this complicates generalisation to a per-patient effect. Second, the two treatment intentions are heterogeneous: thirteen attacks received blockade as acute escalation after inadequate earlier therapy, while five represented early initiation of maintenance. The escalation group is the one where a rescue effect would be most relevant, yet the reported paired comparisons do not specify which subset generated each P value, so the contribution of each intention to the overall improvement is unclear.

Third, the substantial improvement from nadir to pre-blockade (5.0 to 3.5, P=.001) predates the intervention and likely reflects residual effects of corticosteroids, plasma exchange, or spontaneous recovery. The additional drop to 2.0 (P=.03) is therefore measured against an already-improving baseline, not against a stable nadir.

Finally, without a concurrent untreated control group, the P values only indicate that the within-patient change is statistically unlikely under the null of no change; they do not exclude that the same trajectory would have occurred without blockade.
